FAST

LONDON/HONG KONG, Nov 4 : Cryptocurrencies briefly dipped on Wednesday as Democrats won majorities in both the Senate and House in the US midterm elections, a potential blow to an industry that has pushed for faster deregulation for digital assets. The sector has spent more than $300 million backing crypto-friendly Democrats and Republicans in roughly equal measure during the current and previous election cycles, hoping to pass legislation US crypto companies say will put them on a solid legal footing and allow them to thrive. Bitcoin briefly touched a six-week low before recovering to trade roughly flat by 0715 GMT at $78,070. Ether traded at $2,292, up just 1 per cent.  Bitcoin has fallen by around 41 per cent since hitting record highs above $122,000 in October 2025, bringing the value of the broader crypto market to around $2.61 billion, according to CoinMarketCap.

The market has lost some $300 billion in value in the last month alone, as deepening concern about future returns from AI and the strain of rising borrowing costs pushed investors into less risky assets such as government bonds and safe-haven currencies.  Sentiment has also been hurt by the $6 billion hack of the Binance platform last week, the largest heist in history.  On Tuesday, Binance customers had withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened following the hack at the weekend. "The market may be re-evaluating the risk-reward profile of crypto assets. On one hand, the string of security incidents is forcing investors to re-examine the industry's security infrastructure and custody risks," Tim Sun, Senior Researcher at HashKey, said. "On the other hand, potential shifts in the US political landscape could stall the progress of structural crypto legislation and institutional framework development. All of these factors leave the crypto market facing strong headwinds," he said. Trump, who vowed to make the United States the "crypto capital of the world" during his 2024 presidential campaign, has made his own forays into digital assets, with the launch of his "Trump" meme coin, plus his family's World Liberty Financial crypto platform, among other ventures. The sector has seen sweeping reforms in the almost two years since Trump returned to office, including lighter enforcement, the creation of a strategic bitcoin reserve.  Washington has also allowed for easier access to banking and exchange-traded products and passed a federal stablecoin law that could help these assets move into the mainstream payments and money transfer systems.

Source: Reuters

FAST

SEOUL: Twelve South Korean industry groups urged the government on Wednesday (Nov 5) to invest in and support production of Korean television dramas, known as K-dramas, warning that the country's production base risked collapse. K-dramas have been hugely popular globally, but the number produced has fallen about 30 per cent from 141 titles in 2022, according to the Korea Drama Production Association. Three domestic broadcast networks cut drama output from 91 titles in 2012 to 32 in 2023, and some channels had stopped airing weekday dramas altogether, the groups, which represent industry workers including TV drama producers, directors, writers, actors, cinematographers and crew, said. The groups attributed the slump in production to rising production costs, which they linked to competition with well-funded global streaming platforms, broadcasters' reduced capacity to invest, and difficulty securing intellectual property rights.

SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected the construction of a new warship believed to be its latest cruiser and called for modernising the country's shipyards to build a powerful navy, state news agency KCNA said on Wednesday (Nov 4). Kim gave field guidance during the visit to the Nampho Shipyard on the west coast on Monday and said expanding the capacity of the existing shipyards and increasing their operation rate was important to develop the country's marine industry for securing its sea border, according to KCNA. He inspected the construction of a new warship "which is incomparably huge ... compared to the destroyer built last year," KCNA said. North Korea is building its third Choe Hyon-class destroyer under Kim's five-year defence development plan, which aims to produce two surface warships every year.

Photos released by KCNA showed Kim and aides at the lower hull of a vessel supported by massive bilge blocks taller than the men that analysis by the Korea Defense and Security Forum said was the first published image of a 10,000-ton cruiser under construction. The vessel likely will carry a significant number of cruise missiles that will allow longer-range ship-to-surface attack, the Seoul-based think-tank said. Nampho is a major naval shipyard where the North has already constructed a destroyer that satellite images published in October showed is undergoing a major expansion. North Korea has been developing its navy's missile capabilities in recent months, testing anti-ship missiles. In July, Kim observed the test firing of a strategic cruise missile and evaluations of anti-ship systems aboard a naval destroyer. In April, North Korea test-fired anti-warship missiles to assess the efficiency of its destroyer.

SIHANOUKVILLE: After disembarking more than 200 passengers who had paid tens of thousands of dollars to live on board for years, the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship departed Cambodia early on Wednesday (Nov 4). Last week, the vessel's owner, Florida-based Villa Vie Residences, suspended operations and forced passengers off the ship at the port town of Sihanoukville, saying fuel price increases from the Iran war had made operations prohibitively expensive. The ship left with no passengers and around 50 crew, according to Taing Sochitkrishna, head of the Sihanoukville tourism department. He said about 100 passengers remained in Cambodia, while the others largely flew to other destinations in the region. Passengers unloaded their last belongings from the vessel on Tuesday, and many said they did not expect to return to the ship.

"There are still many things on the ship that I wish I could take with me," said Shirine Thomas, of Wilmington, North Carolina, shortly after collecting some final items. The Villa Vie Odyssey had been cruising the world for at least 755 days as one of only a handful of ships that offered passengers the opportunity to rent or buy long-term or even permanent residences on board.

A drone view of the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship departing from Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Preah Sihanouk province, Cambodia, on Nov 4, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Soveit Yarn)

The ship's final destination was unconfirmed. Some passengers and maritime tracking websites indicated the ship was bound for Singapore. Villa Vie Residences did not respond to emails or phone calls seeking comment. Sixty-seven-year-old retired high school teacher Mary Ann Demsar from Ontario, Canada, said the owners had provided no information on whether the voyage would continue. "We don't get any clear indication from the owners of Villa Vie as to what is happening," she said. "They've been so quiet, the only information we get is from the wonderful government and the representatives here in Cambodia."

Source: Reuters/lk

BENGALURU, Nov 4 : India's EloElo Group, the parent of microdrama platform Story TV, said on Wednesday that US entertainment group NBCUniversal and MIT Investment Co were among the investors backing its latest funding round of $80 million. • Microdramas are one of the fastest-growing forms of content globally, and the industry will generate $14 billion in worldwide revenue by the end of 2026, according to research and advisory group Omdia • The funding values the startup at $500 million, said a person with direct knowledge of the matter • The round was led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal, with MIT Investment Co, Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures and Griffin Gaming Partners also participating, the company said
